headline: Net loss narrows sharply as core operating income softens
summary_short: Corebridge's Q2 2026 net loss available to common shareholders narrowed to $16M ($0.04/share) from $660M ($1.20/share) a year ago, while adjusted operating income fell 21% y/y to $664M as shareholders approved the pending Equitable merger on July 30.
summary_long: Net loss available to common shareholders narrowed to $16M ($0.04/share diluted) from $660M ($1.20/share) a year ago, driven mainly by lower realized investment losses, partly offset by unfavorable market-risk-benefit fair-value changes and higher interest credited to policyholders. Adjusted pre-tax operating income (APTOI) fell 21% y/y to $664M (-2% ex-variable investment income) on higher policyholder benefits and interest credited, partly offset by higher premiums and investment income. Premiums and deposits fell 13% y/y to $9.1B on lower fixed-annuity sales. The company returned $412M to shareholders ($300M buybacks, $112M dividends) and declared a $0.25/share dividend. Shareholders approved the pending Equitable merger on July 30. No forward guidance was found in the release.

Net loss narrowed to $16M from $660M a year ago, driven mainly by lower realized losses, partly offset by unfavorable changes in market risk benefit fair value and higher interest credited to policyholders.
Swung to a $52M pre-tax profit from a $608M pre-tax loss a year ago; the release ties the after-tax net-loss narrowing behind this to lower realized investment losses.
Loss per share narrowed to $0.04 from $1.20 a year ago, tracking the net-loss narrowing described above and aided by a 17.5% y/y drop in diluted share count from continued buybacks.
CEO Marc Costantini called Q2 execution strong and said shareholder approval of the Equitable merger on July 30 was a "pivotal milestone" toward final execution and value creation.
